questions.prompt: Which module must you import to use ngModel, ngForm, and ngModelGroup?
questions.explanation: Template-driven form directives come from FormsModule; add it to the standalone component's imports array.

questions.prompt: Why is the name attribute required on an ngModel input inside a <form>?

options.text: Angular uses it as the key to register the control within the form's FormGroup
It is only needed for styling

questions.explanation: Without name (and without standalone options), Angular can't register the control and throws a runtime error.

questions.prompt: The [(ngModel)] "banana in a box" syntax is shorthand for which combination?
questions.explanation: [(ngModel)]="x" expands to [ngModel]="x" (ngModelChange)="x = $event" — property binding in, event binding out.

questions.prompt: When should validation error messages be shown for the best UX?

options.text: Only after the field is touched and/or dirty
Only after the form is submitted successfully
Never — rely on the disabled button

questions.explanation: Gating messages behind touched/dirty avoids scolding users before they've interacted with the field.

questions.prompt: Which directive groups related controls into a nested FormGroup (e.g. an address block)?
questions.explanation: ngModelGroup="address" produces a nested form value like { address: { street, city } } that mirrors your data model.

questions.prompt: Even with [disabled]="form.invalid" on the submit button, why should onSubmit re-check form.invalid?

options.text: A disabled button can be bypassed, so it is not real validation/security

questions.explanation: Disabling the button is only UX; always re-validate in the handler (and on the server).
